rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human mercy begins as an affective tenderness toward the afflicted and aims to remove harm and establish good; sometimes a word or gesture suffices, while its complete end is voluntary beneficence.
rows.anchor: bir iyilik duygusudur demiştik, ki bu ibtidâ şefkat gibi teessür ve infi‘âl kabîlinden bir meyl-i nefsânî olarak başlar

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In ordinary speech, calling someone merciful usually means tender-hearted capacity, while calling them very merciful points to visible beneficial action.
rows.anchor: ekseriyâ “rikkat-i kalb” dediğimiz hâlet-i rûhiyeyi, kābiliyyet-i infi‘âliyeyi kastederiz, fakat “pek merhametli, çok merhametli” dediğimiz zaman da netîce-i fi‘liyesinin zuhûrunu anlarız

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because God is beyond change and affect, divine mercy cannot be explained as the same psychological state as human compassion; both rational and revealed indications support this.
rows.anchor: Cenâb-ı Allah ise ‘alâim-i hudûs olan tegayyür ve infi‘alden

rows.speaker: müfessirîn
rows.claim: Exegetes allow some lexical metaphor in divine mercy: either its necessary result, deliverance and beneficence, or the prior will of good that causes beneficence.
rows.anchor: müfessirîn burada az çok bir mecâz-ı lügavî bulunduğunu söylerler ki bu da iki suretle mülâhaza edilir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the first interpretation mercy is an attribute of action; on the second, the will of good is an essential attribute, since willing is choice rather than affect.
rows.anchor: evvelkine göre rahmet sıfat-ı fiilden, ikinciye göre sıfat-ı zâtiyeden olur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since divine mercy is perfect and both adjectives occur, he prefers including both the essential will of good and its acts of beneficence.
rows.anchor: burada iki mânayı da kastetmek daha muvâfıktır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He explains Rahmân as a special, stable adjective for God's essential will of good, and Rahîm as an intensive active participle for its manifested beneficence; some reverse this mapping.
rows.anchor: “Rahmân” sıfat-ı hâssa olduğuna nazaran garîze ve sübut ifade eden sıfat-ı müşebbehe olarak irâde-i hayr sıfat-ı zâtiyesi, “Rahîm” de mübalağa ile ism-i fâil

rows.speaker: Bunu aks edenler
rows.claim: Some interpreters reverse the allocation of essential and active meanings between Rahmân and Rahîm.
rows.anchor: Bunu aks edenler de olmuştur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His preferred account treats divine names and attributes as literally true, not metaphorical, while recognizing that their divine meanings are not identical to human ones.
rows.anchor: bizim muhtârımız şudur ki sıfât ve esmâ-i ilâhiye mânalarında mecaz değil, hakikattirler

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Divine knowledge and will are eternal creator-attributes and the source of human counterparts; human acquisition, desire, and temporal change are incidental conditions, not their essence.
rows.anchor: İlm-i ilâhî ve irâde-i ilâhiye ise bizim bu sıfatlarımızın

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He distinguishes divine rahmet from human merhamet in Turkish, so translating Rahmân Rahîm simply as “very compassionate” is inadequate.
rows.anchor: “Rahmet”i ilâhî; “merhamet”i beşerî bir mânada kullanırız

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A fuller explanation is boundless mercy and beneficent outpouring, combining the essential will of good with rescue from harm and delivery to blessings.
rows.anchor: nâmütenâhî rahmet sâhibi, nâmütenâhî feyz-i in‘âm, hayr u ihsan saçıcı” diye bir îzah yapabiliriz

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Harm is rooted in nonexistence and its causes, good in existence and its causes; pains warn of lost good, while pleasures announce a share in existence.
rows.anchor: âfâtın hakikati ‘adem ve sevâik-i ‘ademdir, hayrâtın hakikati de vücûd ve sevâik-i vücûddur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Despair of God and His mercy is the root of suffering, while faith in God and His mercy is the root of pleasure and hope.
rows.anchor: Bunların başı Hak’tan ve rahmet-i Hak’tan yeistir. Ni‘am ve hayrât ile alâkadar olan bütün lezzetlerimiz

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worldly life is a renewed struggle between nonbeing and being, pain and pleasure, despair and faith, sustained by divine mercy and human effort; the afterlife eternally separates their outcomes.
rows.anchor: Hayât-ı dünyâ böyle ‘adem ile vücûdun, âlâm ile lezâizin, yeis ile imanın, rahmet-i Rahmân ve sa‘y u te‘âvün ile yenilen bir mücadelesi şeklidir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human good begins with being brought from nonexistence and culminates in passing from the finite to the infinite.
rows.anchor: Binâen‘aleyh bizim hayr ve lezâizimizin başlangıcı ‘ademden vücûda

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rahmân's mercy is God's will to bring every possible thing from nonexistence into existence, because existence is the source of every good and blessing.
rows.anchor: Rahmet-i rahmâniye bütün mümkinâtın ‘ademden vücûda ihrâcını ifade eden irâde-i vücûd ve in‘âm-ı vücûd olduğundan

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rahmân creates human bodily and spiritual existence and supplies the provisions that sustain life; no creature falls outside this encompassing mercy.
rows.anchor: bizi cismâniyet ve rûhâniyetimizle ‘ademden vücûda getirerek halk eden ve bununla beraber esbâb-ı bekā ve hayâtımız olan nimetleri de ihzar ve îsâl eyleyen

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The full scope of Rahmân's mercy includes creating beings who can reason and act by choice.
rows.anchor: âkil ve bi’l-ihtiyâr fâil olacak mevcûdât halk eylemek de rahmet-i rahmâniyenin kemâl-i şümûlü muktezâsındandır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Multiple independent wills would introduce an accidental plurality that undermines lasting existence, since God's partner is intrinsically false and nonexistent.
rows.anchor: iradelerin ta‘addüdü hasebiyle vücûdda bir nevi şirk-i ‘arazî zuhur eder. Hâlbuki şirk ile vücûd ve devâm-ı vücûd mümteni‘dir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Natural and moral evils ultimately grow from multiplicity and claims of partnership, because divine unity is necessary for existence.
rows.anchor: âlemde gerek tabîî ve gerek ahlâkī ne kadar şürûr tasavvur edilirse hepsinin kökü ta‘addüd ve da‘vâ-yı şirktir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rahîm's mercy preserves balance by governing the many free wills through one divine will, sustaining existence while allowing choice.
rows.anchor: bütün tecelliyât-ı vücûdu bir irade ile idare ve idâme etmek öyle dakīk bir nimet ve öyle ebedî bir hayırdır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Perfect divine nurture balances necessity with choice; philosophers call this delicate reconciliation the riddle of existence.
rows.anchor: Kemâl-i terbiye îcab ile ihtiyârın işte bu ihtilâtındaki muvâzenede ve kemâl-i rabbânî felâsifenin “mu‘ammâ-yı vücûd” dedikleri bu mu‘âdele-i rahîmiyededir

rows.speaker: eslâf-ı müfessirîn
rows.claim: Earlier exegetes call Rahîm's mercy the subtleties of blessings and also interpret it by the blessings of the afterlife.
rows.anchor: eslâf-ı müfessirîn rahmet-i rahîmiyeye “dekāik-i ni‘am” tâbir etmişler ve gaye itibariyle da ni‘am-ı uhreviye ile tefsir etmişlerdir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God gives each person a share of choice, then judges acquired rights on the true balance and assigns reward or punishment for even an atom's worth; punishment safeguards reward, whose primary aim is mercy.
rows.anchor: فَمَن يَعْمَلْ مِثْقَالَ ذَرَّةٍ خَيْرًۭا يَرَهُۥ وَمَن يَعْمَلْ مِثْقَالَ ذَرَّةٍۢ شَرًّۭا يَرَهُۥ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Initial existence under Rahmân keeps creatures on their course; a second existence under Rahîm concerns free agents, some of whom depart from duty and upset the balance through choice.
rows.anchor: Rahmet-i rahmâniye içindeki vücûd-i ibtidâîde hiçbir mevcud yolundan inhiraf etmez. Rahmet-i rahîmiye içindeki vücûd-i sânî ise ashâb-ı irâdeye ait olduğundan

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's own Rahmânic will remains sovereign over the general balance of justice and mercy.
rows.anchor: bu mu‘âdelenin mîzân-ı umûmîsinde de lâ-şerîke leh olan Hak teâlâ’nın

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse about the Merciful established over the Throne illustrates this encompassing divine governance.
rows.anchor: ٱلرَّحْمَٰنُ عَلَى ٱلْعَرْشِ ٱسْتَوَىٰ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rahmân gives existence and its sustaining blessings to all rational beings whether or not they seek them; Rahîm addresses their voluntary striving and offers greater, desired gifts by God's will.
rows.anchor: er-Rahmân diyor ki: Ey zevi’l-‘ukūl! Siz isteseniz de istemeseniz de

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rational beings are created to reflect divine mercy through their own will, draw near to God, and attain the greatest favor; they remain accountable for choices that threaten shared existence.
rows.anchor: Ey zevi’l-‘ukūl! Ey ashâb-ı irâde! Siz diğerleri gibi değilsiniz, onlar sade irâde-i rahmâniyenin ceberûtuna mahkumdurlar

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God calls people away from denial and associationism toward loving, upright work for truth, justice, mercy, and eternal reward.
rows.anchor: Haydi Hakk’ı inkâr etmeyiniz, şirk koşmayınız, Hakk’a kurbiyet ve hatta niyâbet için hak ve irâde-i hak yolunda mahabbetle

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Divine lordship is not merely coercive destruction: it increases blessings through mercy; the cited verse promises good and more to those who do good.
rows.anchor: Benim rubûbiyetim kahr u ceberûttan ibaret bir tasarruf-ı tazyîk ve i‘dâm değil, böyle rahmâniyet ve rahîmiyet ile tezyîd-i in‘âm eden bir rubûbiyet-i celîle ve cemîledir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He raises and rejects the thought that after creating free agents, God delegated future outcomes to them and withdrew, leaving them masters of reward, punishment, and the future.
rows.anchor: Acaba Rabbü’l-âlemin ashâb-ı irâdeyi halk ettikten sonra istikbalin mukadderâtını onlara tefvîz etmiş ve kendisi acaba hicâb-ı izzete çekilmiş değil midir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This conceit mistakes limited present choice for absolute creative power and unrestricted freedom, a claim of partnership that underlies human calamity and injustice.
rows.anchor: irâde-i cüz’iyeye mutlak bir irâde-i külliye ve her kayıttan âzâde bir ihtiyar ve bir kudret-i hâlıka kıymeti isnad ederek kendilerini kādir-i kül

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Without divine justice and mercy regulating this arrogance, human society would destroy itself; the verse links corruption on land and sea to people's deeds.
rows.anchor: rahmet-i ilâhiyenin bunun üzerindeki ta‘dîlâtı, inzibâtı olmasa cem‘iyyet-i beşeriye üç gün içinde birbirini yer bitirir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: New creation continually occurs beyond human will; paralysis can instantly humble the strongest, and the preserved mummies of Pharaohs show that past rulers no longer own their former might.
rows.anchor: Hâlbuki âlemde ve hele hayatta her an irâde-i beşerden hâriç halk-ı cedîd cereyan etmekte olduğu cihetle kuvveti kendisinin zanneden o kavî pazuları bir an içinde

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God holds the reins of existence and life in past and future alike: He is both First and Last, while the first agent and ultimate end are truly one.
rows.anchor: ve O’nun milkidir. O zannedildiği gibi sadece Evvel değil, hem Evvel ve hem Âhir’dir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The spherical bodies and cycles of time suggest this unity through their center and circumference.
rows.anchor: ecrâmın küriyyeti, zamanın istidâresi merkez ve muhîtinden bize bunu iş‘âr eder

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some who sense God's control extend compulsion even to the present; human beings alternately boast “all me” in strength and appeal to another in weakness.
rows.anchor: Bu noktayı hissedenlerin bir kısmı mâzî ve istikbal şöyle d ursun, hâlde bile cebr-i mahza kāil olmuşlardır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The truth is neither pure determinism nor pure autonomy, but a middle position between the two.
rows.anchor: hakikat ise ne öyle ne böyledir, أَمْر بَيْنَ أَمْرَيْن’dir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human life combines body and spirit, reason and heart, capacity and action, necessity and choice; humans are neither absolutely compelled nor absolutely self-acting.
rows.anchor: Beşeriyet cisim ile rûhun, akıl ile kalbin, kābiliyet ile fâiliyetin, ıztırar ile ihtiyârın muhassalasıdır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Both strict determinists and advocates of complete creative freedom fail to fit the evident balance of reality.
rows.anchor: müdde‘îlerinin ihtiyâr-ı hâlikāne dâvaları, hiçbir zaman mîzân-ı hakīkatin bedâhetiyle karşılaşamazlar

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Necessity in humans witnesses God's power, while their capacity to choose witnesses God's will; humans are brought into existence by God yet may choose their striving through divine mercy.
rows.anchor: Beşerde cihet-i ıztırar kudretullâhın şâhidi, cihet-i ihtiyar da irâdetullâhın şâhididir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A person's present authority is a temporary, limited, borrowed trust and delegated commission from God, neither to be denied nor mistaken for an unremovable absolute title.
rows.anchor: müsâ‘ade-i Hakk’a mazhar bir salâhiyet-i niyâbiyeyi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People receive future reward and punishment rather than distribute it; when their borrowed means are withdrawn, they receive as needy dependents, not owners.
rows.anchor: İnsan istikbaldeki mükâfat ve mücâzâtı verecek değil, alacaktır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Absolute ownership of the heavens, earth, times, beings, matter, forces, capacities, and actions belongs to God as creator and sustainer.
rows.anchor: bütün âlemînin mâliki, mübdi‘i, hâlıkı, mürebbîsi olan Allah teâlâ’nın milk-i mutlakıdır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling God Master of the Day of Recompense removes the lingering idea that people could own or rule the day of reward and punishment.
rows.anchor: O hâlde mâzînin mâliki Allah iken hâlin ve istikbalin, bugünün ve yarının bilfiil mâliki ve sâhibi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arabic dīn can mean recompense, account, judgment, governance, obedience, custom, condition, domination, or the religion and law tied to these; it does not directly mean resurrection.
rows.anchor: “din” kelimesi lisân-ı Arab’da cezâ,

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He recognizes two sound readings here: dīn as recompense, and dīn in its familiar sense of religion.
rows.anchor: burada evvelki cezâ, sonuncu dîn-i ma‘rûf mânalarıyla iki tefsîr-i mu‘teber vardır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Recompense includes future accountability, awareness of responsibility, and its actual enforcement.
rows.anchor: Evvelâ cezâ, âtîde mes’ûliyet, hiss-i mes’ûliyet, tatbîk-i mes’ûliyet mânalarını da tazammun eder

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jazāʾ means giving the sweet or painful return and reward for good or bad deeds, not punishment alone; the prayer asks God for much good reward.
rows.anchor: aslında “cezâ” kelimesi şimdi müte‘âref olduğu gibi yalnız ‘ikāb ve ukūbet demek olmayıp iyi veya kötü yapılan bir işin tatlı veya acı karşılığını

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because “reward” and “requital” suggest reciprocal equality, sacred usage avoids ascribing these terms to God and instead says reward, punishment, recompense, or payment.
rows.anchor: “mükâfat” ve “mücâzat” kelimeleri küfüv ve müşareket mânalarını ifham ettiğinden lisân-ı şer‘de Cenâb-ı Allah’a isnad olunmaz

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yawm al-dīn is the final time when every deed receives its return and rewards and punishments are distributed; it is also called the Last Day and includes judgment.
rows.anchor: istikbalde mükâfat ve mücâzâtın tevzî‘olunacağı vakit demektir ki lisân-ı şer‘de buna “yevm-i âhir” dahi denilir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Day” means a period of time, not necessarily daytime, nighttime, or a twenty-four-hour cycle; it may use any known or unknown measure of time.
rows.anchor: bu gibi yerlerde “yevm” ve “gün” kelimelerinin ‘ale’l-ıtlâk vakit mânasına kullanıldığı da mâlumdur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Day of Recompense is the final certainty when hopes and despair pass through God's balance and divide into eternal bliss or loss; it refers to Resurrection by implication, not as the lexical meaning of dīn.
rows.anchor: Bundan sonrası artık ya gāye-i ümîd olan ebedî rıdvân-ı ekber veya gāye-i ye’s olan ebedî hüsrân-ı ekberdir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Resurrection encompasses revival, gathering, standing, questioning, accounting, the balance, the bridge, and finally the distribution of reward or punishment.
rows.anchor: ba‘s, haşr u cem‘, vakfe yani tevakkuf ve intizar, sual, hesab, mîzan, sırât, nihâyet bütün amellerin iyiye iyi sevâbının

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Replacing “Day of Recompense” with “Day of Resurrection,” “Questioning,” or “Account” weakens the verse's stated goal and its exhortation and warning.
rows.anchor: burada “yevmü’d-dîn” nazmıyla bu gaye tasrih edilerek tergīb ve terhîbe kuvvet verilmiştir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording establishes belief in the afterlife indirectly: “religion” is hinted by the word choice and by the reference to reward and punishment, though dīn here is not used in its familiar sense.
rows.anchor: “din” kelimesini ma‘nâ-yı ma‘rûfunda kullanmamış ve ona dolayısıyla işaret ve îmâ etmiştir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In its familiar sense, religion is a divine ordinance that leads rational beings toward intrinsic good by their free choice.
rows.anchor: Din, zevi’l-‘ukūlü hüsn-i ihtiyarlarıyla bi’z-zât hayırlara sevk eden bir vaz‘-ı ilâhîdir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This definition describes true religion, whose guidance genuinely leads to good; false religions provide only an illusory route toward claimed or relative good and thereby disclose their nature.
rows.anchor: dîn-i hakkın bir târifidir. Çünkü bi’z-zât hayra sevk-i hakīkī ancak ondadır. Edyân-ı bâtılada ise bu sevk vehmî olur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The definition identifies religion's proper subjects, conditions, results, and pillars, and its legal meaning gathers the word's lexical meanings.
rows.anchor: dinin mahalli, şerâiti, semeresi, erkânı, yani cinsi ve fasl-ı mümeyyizi gösterilmiştir ve bu ma‘nâ-yı şer‘î “din” kelimesinin bütün me‘ânî-i lügaviyesini câmi‘dir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: True religion addresses rational beings; inanimate things, plants, animals, the insane, children, and those with impaired understanding are not its proper subjects, though calling animals religious is metaphorical.
rows.anchor: Dîn-i hakkın mahalli, akıl sahipleridir. Binâen‘aleyh cemâdât, nebâtât, hayvânât, mecnunlar, gayr-i âkiller, çocuklar, ma‘tûhlar gibi kāsırîn tecelliyât-ı dîniyeye mahal değildir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reason and choice are conditions of religion: without reason there can be no religious address or obligation, and without choice religion cannot guide and influence a person.
rows.anchor: Dinin şartı akıl ve ihtiyardır. Bunlar dinin şartı, diyânetin rüknüdürler

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Learning and rationality alone do not make a person religious; one must both know and love the religion.
rows.anchor: Fi’l-vâki‘âlim ve âkil olmak mütedeyyin olmaya kâfi değildir. Dindar olmak için dini hem bilmek ve hem sevmek lâzımdır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The noun “religion” names the objective divine law, while “religiosity” is the human quality and voluntary acquisition that applies it; confusing them leads to error.
rows.anchor: din vaz‘-ı ilâhî, diyanet kesb-i beşerîdir. Bunu tefrik edemeyenler ilim nâmına hatalara düşerler

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Religion's fruit is deeds that are genuinely beneficial by God's measure, not merely by the doer's own opinion; piety means choosing good because God regards it as good.
rows.anchor: asıl dindarlık hayrı nazar-ı Hak’ta hayr olduğu için ihtiyar edip yapmaktır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Good is what benefits another now or in the future; doing something because it is intrinsically good is evidently doing it for God.
rows.anchor: Hayr ise hakikatte umûmî olsun, husûsî olsun âhara hâlen veya istikbâlen nâfi‘olandır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Every deed good in God's sight surely has a reward, whose greatest form is God's approval; God is the source and guarantor of all good, reward, and blessing.
rows.anchor: Hak teâlâ ‘indinde hayr olan her işin de bir ecri, bir sevâbı, bir mükâfâtı muhakkaktır. Ve bunun en büyüğü O’nun rızâsıdır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Doing good for immediate personal gain is a transaction seeking payment from people, not an act for the sake of good; asking reward from God recognizes the right and the good.
rows.anchor: Bu ise hayrı hayr olduğu için yapmak ve Hak ile bir muâmele icrâ etmek değildir. Ecrini Hak’tan isteyerek yapmak ise

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Doing good while considering its afterlife reward is a higher degree of perfection, and no good is ever lost with God.
rows.anchor: Fakat bu ecri sade âhirette mülâhaza ederek yapmak daha yüksek bir mertebe-i kemâldir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Without recognizing God and standing for truth, people cannot fully recognize or love good for its own sake; love of good begins with love of truth, and sincerity requires truthfulness.
rows.anchor: hubb-i hayrın başı hubb-i haktır ve samimiyet ve ihlâsın şart-ı evveli hakperestliktir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: True religion is divine in origin; other human institutions serve personal interests and can foster evil, association, and conflict rather than intrinsically good action.
rows.anchor: mevzu‘ât-ı sâire zât-ı Hakk’a muzâf değildir ve ağrâz-ı şahsiye ile ma‘lûldür

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Divine origin is recognized through evidence of God's knowledge, will, and approval, above all God's speech in the Qur'an, which heart and reason understand necessarily or by inference.
rows.anchor: Bunların en kuvvetlisi Kur’an gibi hitâbullahtır. Kalb ve akıl bu hitabı bi’z-zarûre veya bi’l-istidlâl fehm ü telakkī eyler

rows.speaker: bazı feylesoflar
rows.claim: Some philosophers consider the felt taste of conscience sufficient to identify divine religion.
rows.anchor: Bu noktada bazı feylesoflar zevk-i vicdânı kâfi görmüşler

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Conscience is too personal and varied to define a single true religion; one must look beyond it toward universal conscience or a universal spirit as a measure.
rows.anchor: âlemde her şahsın kendine mahsus bir zevk-i vicdânı vardır. Ve o hâlde ferdler kadar da din vardır demek lâzım gelir

rows.speaker: diğer bazıları
rows.claim: Others appeal only to reason, supposing it the sole judge of truth and good because it is not personal and follows one path.
rows.anchor: Diğer bazıları yalnız akla müracaat etmişler ve aklın hak ve hayrda hâkim-i yegâne olduğunu zannetmişlerdir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reason is the best instrument of understanding, but cannot govern the heart or encompass the whole spirit, so it remains a secondary, nonsovereign aid in grasping divine law.
rows.anchor: ahvâl-i kalbde hâkim olmadığından rûhun bütün mevcûdiyetine intibak edemez

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Divine law must first appear to the whole human spirit as self-evident necessary knowledge, unmistakably recognized as God's ordinance, before reason and heart draw from it.
rows.anchor: ile tecellî etmelidir ki bu tecellî bizzat Hakk’ın vaz‘u hitâbı olduğu

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sacred law calls this necessary knowledge “revelation” and the recipient's realization “prophethood.”
rows.anchor: bu ilm-i zarûrîye lisân-ı şer‘de “vahiy”, ve bu mazhariyete “nübüvvet” ıtlak olunur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The chief difference between divine and human ordinances is whether human will causes the ordinance, not whether its manifestation occurs outside humanity.
rows.anchor: vaz‘-ı ilâhî ile vaz‘-ı beşerînin en mühim farkı o mevzû‘un tecellîsinde irâde-i beşerin âmil olup olmamasına râci‘dir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: True religion is first fixed in primordial nature through an unacquired necessity expressing God's will, then disclosed to a holy spirit through certain witnessed knowledge containing the principles of proof.
rows.anchor: evvelâ levh-i mahfûz-i fıtratta kesbî olmayan ve irâdetullâhı gösteren bir ıztırar ile sâbit olur da

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After revelation, its necessary knowledge develops through empirical and historical verification, rational inference, and inward experience; revelation has an analogue in conscience and a proof in reason.
rows.anchor: bir taraftan tevsîk-i tecribî ve târihî, diğer taraftan istidlâlât-ı akliye ve ezvâk-ı kalbiye ile tarîk-i kesbden inkişaf ve ta‘ammüm eder gider

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At revelation the spirit is wholly absorbed in direct witnessing, with voluntary activity temporarily interrupted, and perceives dimensions of existence beyond reason's reach.
rows.anchor: rûh bütün mevcûdiyetiyle şuhûda müstağrak olarak kābil-i mahz kesilir ve fâ‘iliyyet-i irâdiyesi ve kuvânın hususiyetleri muvakkaten munkatı‘olur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: True religion begins through prophethood as a divine ordinance manifested in a human recipient; the human spirit receives God's knowledge rather than producing it.
rows.anchor: Doğrusu, rûh-i beşer ilm-i Hak’ta fâil değil kābildir. Ma‘lûmat uydurulmaz, alınır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ideas produced with human choice can be mistaken, whereas certain knowledge is a divine placement; religious law requires detachment from self-interest and desire.
rows.anchor: Rûhun kendinde ihtiyârını karıştırarak imâl ettiği fikirlerde ise ilim

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Desire, greed, and passion cloud reason and the heart, so freedom from them is essential to knowledge of religion; a cited hadith warns against interpreting the Qur'an by personal opinion.
rows.anchor: Garaz, hırs, teşehhî kalb ve aklı sislendirir, çeşm-i basîreti şaşı yapar. Ya hiç göstermez veya çatal gösterir

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: A hadith cited by the author says that whoever interprets the Qur'an by personal opinion has disbelieved.
rows.anchor: مَنْ فَسَّرَ الْقُرْآنَ بِرَأْ�ِهِ فَقَدْ كَفَرَ “Kur’ân’ı re’yi ile tefsir eden kâfir olur”

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Revelation gives the most self-evident certainty as a necessary divine communication, beyond ordinary knowledge and untouched by acquisition or desire, confirmed by rational proofs and contemporary experience.
rows.anchor: hiçbir şâibe-i kesb u i‘mâl ve hiçbir nişâne-i teşehhî olmaksızın rûhun kābiliyyet-i sırfesi üzerinde zâhir ve bâtınından tam bir telkīn-i zarûrî ile vaz‘-ı ilâhîyi veren

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Revelation is beyond voluntary activity but not beyond innate receptivity; afterward, true religion enters reason's inductive knowledge, where discovery precedes theory.
rows.anchor: her müşahede gibi kalb ve aklın fâ‘iliyyet-i ihtiyâriyesi fevkinde olmakla beraber kābiliyyet-i fıtriyesinden de hâriç değildir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Individual experience cannot encompass all religious truth; the unity of God is the one foundation that can be directly experienced in full.
rows.anchor: bunda tecribe-i ferdiye hepsini ihâtaya kâfi değildir. O ancak aslü’l-usûl olan tevhîd-i Hak’da mümkin olabilir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Many important religious and legislative truths require repeated observation over centuries, making reason and transmitted authority both important.
rows.anchor: Hakāik-i dîniye ve mesâil-i teşrî‘iyede tekerrür müşahedesi, tecribesi asırlara mütevakkıf nice metâlib-i mühimme vardır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Islam recognizes four proofs for divine ordinance: Qur'an, Sunna, community consensus, and analogy; the first three establish, while analogy discloses.
rows.anchor: İslâm’da da vaz‘-ı ilâhîyi bildiren delil dörttür. Kitâb, sünnet, icmâ‘-ı ümmet, kıyastır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: True religion is a formative law that makes rational people freely choose good and become agents of happiness; its guidance is not necessary or coercive.
rows.anchor: dîn-i hak zorla değil seve seve hayr yapan fâ‘il-i muhtar insanlar yetiştiren bir kānûn-ı terbiyedir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Religion encourages choice by showing good and bad outcomes; the declaration that there is no compulsion in religion follows because forced good belongs to the coercer, not the compelled person.
rows.anchor: Bunun için “dinde cebir yoktur” denilir لَآ إِكْرَاهَ فِى ٱلدِّينِ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even a learned person is not affected by true religion without choice and religious practice; mutual support for God is tied to divine support.
rows.anchor: Din ne kadar hak olursa olsun câhilinde bu suretle

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Without chosen religious goodness, a person remains either an instrument forced by others or an agent of evil and corruption.
rows.anchor: Bu hüsn-i ihtiyâra, bu diyânete sâhip olmayanlar, ya diğerlerinin cebriyle hayra sürüklenen ve hürriyetine mâlik olamayarak onların âlet-i icrâiyesi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Religion's own guidance differs from compelling someone toward religion: rational necessity does not by itself cause action, whose cause is will and power.
rows.anchor: dinin sevki başka, dine sevk yine başkadır. İlim gibi dinin de sevki cebrî değildir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Guardianship can sometimes direct people coercively toward good, as in parents' upbringing and commanding right and forbidding wrong; choice is a condition for religion's effect but a component of religiosity.
rows.anchor: ebeveynin evlâdı sevk ve terbiyesi, emr bi’l-ma‘rûf ve nehy ‘ani’l-münker mesâili bu kabīldendir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Religion is the full set of laws of truth and good offered to reason and choice as faith and practice, also called millet and sharia; religiosity is their voluntary application.
rows.anchor: din, iman ve amel mevzû‘u olarak akıl ve ihtiyâra teklif olunacak hak ve hayr kanunlarının hey’et-i mecmû‘asıdır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although whether deeds form part of faith has been debated, he concludes that deeds are a consequence rather than a component; faith and action both belong to religiosity, and their laws are pillars of religion.
rows.anchor: doğrusu amel imanın cüz’ü değil, bir semere-i müterettibesi olduğu tahkik olunmuş ise de

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A religion's truth is confirmed when complete practice fulfills its promised goods and happiness; false religions' promises vary inversely with practice.
rows.anchor: bir dinin hakkiyeti diyânet-i kâmile şartıyla umûma vaad ettiği hayırların, saadetlerin tahakkuku ile tebeyyün edecektir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Islamic history since the Prophet's era supports this claim: sincere religious adherence increased understanding and practice of true good, blessing, and happiness for Muslims and those around them.
rows.anchor: Ta asr-ı sa‘âdetten beri Müslümanlar ne zaman dinlerine diyânet-i sâdıka ile sarılmışlarsa hayr-ı hakīkīyi anlamışlar ve yapmışlar

rows.speaker: bazı Avrupalılar
rows.claim: Some Europeans argue that modern people value utility rather than intrinsic good, no longer feel motivated by divine religion, and must be driven by self-interest, human-made religion, mechanical laws, and coercive force.
rows.anchor: Asr-ı hâzır insanları saadeti nef‘ü hayrda değil intifâ‘da görüyor. Bizzat bir hak ve bizzat bir hayr tanımıyor

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He says this diagnosis concedes that true religion is right and that those who reject its reward deserve its punishment, admitting the harmful results of associationism described in the verse about corruption.
rows.anchor: Böyle demek “dîn-i hak doğru imiş, haksızlar onun sevâbına değil ‘ikābına lâyıktırlar” demeye müsâvîdir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People who refuse divine unity and mercy deserve these painful results; God also manifests Himself through this majestic, forceful lordship.
rows.anchor: Bu da tevhîd-i Hak ile Rahmân-ı Rahîm’e sarılmayan insanların hakk-ı zâtîleri ve binâen‘aleyh Rabbü’l-âlemîn’in bir eser-i celâl

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Only the present trial of conflict and the future Day of Recompense, with its rewards and punishments, can overcome self-interested greed.
rows.anchor: hâldeki ibtilâ-yı cidâl ile istikbâldeki yevmü’d-dînin mükâfat ve mücâzâtını duymak yenecektir

rows.speaker: Kant
rows.claim: Kant inferred God's necessary existence from the necessary existence of the afterlife by practical reason.
rows.anchor: ile âhiretin vücûb-i vücûdundan istintâc etmiştir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The afterlife is an important foundation of religion, and belief in it is a foundation of religiosity; the Day of Recompense belongs especially to religion.
rows.anchor: yevm-i âhiret dinin ve ona iman diyânetin bir asl-ı mühimmini teşkil eder. Ve o günün dine böyle bir ihtisâsı vardır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Explicitly naming God Master of the Day of Recompense makes the promise and warning especially eloquent: religion has such a day.
rows.anchor: âyetinde bu tebşir ve inzârın tasrîhi bu haysiyetle de pek beliğ olmuştur Dinin böyle bir günü vardır

rows.speaker: bazı müfessirîn
rows.claim: Some exegetes cited by Ibn Jarir take dīn here in its familiar sense of religion, millet, or sharia, making the phrase the known important day of religion and thereby referring directly to the afterlife and Resurrection.
rows.anchor: tefsirinde nakledildiği üzere bazı müfessirîn buradaki dini sade mükâfat ve mücâzat mânasına değil

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The recompense interpretation is more apparent at the beginning of the discourse, while the religion interpretation comes immediately to mind at its conclusion; he therefore preserves both in the translation “Master of the day of religion.”
rows.anchor: İbtidâ’-i hitâba nazaran evvelki zâhir, intihâ’-i hitâba nazaran da ikinci mütebâdirdir. Bunun için biz de bu iki mefhûmu zâyi‘etmemek için meâlinde “din gününün mâliki” demeliyiz
